page: Amazon Web Services c9g.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance running on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by the arm64 AWS Graviton processor family using ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 cores clocked at 3.3 GHz, it features 4 dedicated vCPUs with a 1:1 physical-core-to-thread allocation. The server is configured with 8.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache. There is no bundled local storage or integrated GPU acceleration, and baseline network performance is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-threaded performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core execution (2351.0), Geekbench text processing (3079.0), single-threaded gzip compression (36.57 GB/sec), and PassMark memory testing (3281.9). Multi-core throughput remains mid-tier across stress-ng tests (8025.08) and Geekbench multi-core workloads (7671.0). PassMark CPU metrics register lower, reflecting the absence of x86 instruction extensions and standard ARM cryptographic profiling differences.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the c9g.xlarge emphasizes compute density over memory capacity. Workloads requiring large in-memory footprints or heavy vector instruction acceleration will face constraints, and local disk caching is not supported due to the absence of local storage. However, the dedicated physical cores and efficient architecture make this instance well suited for web serving, microservices, code compilation pipelines, compression tasks, and lightweight database handling.
